It uses EuroSCORE (not RCRI) as an illustrative example for coronary artery bypass grafting. It does not report on RCRI validation with biomarkers in noncardiac surgery patients.

This is a clinical practice guideline document summarizing evidence-based recommendations. While it may discuss RCRI, it is not a primary validation study of RCRI with biomarkers. Guidelines are secondary sources that synthesize existing evidence rather than original research validating prediction models.

The population (cancer patients) and context (oncology prognosis) do not match the review protocol requiring adult patients undergoing noncardiac surgery.

This is a statistical methodology paper about interpreting random effects meta-analyses. It has no relevance to RCRI, biomarkers, or noncardiac surgery. It is purely methodological content about meta-analysis techniques.

The title explicitly states it investigates 'the added value of different biomarkers to the Revised Cardiac Risk Index' for predicting MACE and all-cause mortality after noncardiac surgery. This aligns perfectly with the selection criteria requiring RCRI validation with addition of biomarkers in adults undergoing noncardiac surgery.
